claims.text: The initial refractory high-entropy alloy has a uniform BCC matrix.
The initial alloy has good room-temperature performance.
The initial alloy has limited high-temperature strength.
Adding approximately 1–2 at.% Ti and applying an optimized aging treatment will produce coherent Ti-rich nanoprecipitates.
The Ti-rich nanoprecipitates will be uniformly distributed within the BCC matrix.
Coherent Ti-rich nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion from the nanoprecipitates will increase elevated-temperature yield strength through precipitation strengthening.
The nanoprecipitates will not undergo substantial coarsening under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
The Ti addition and heat treatment will preserve room-temperature ductility and mechanical performance.
Limiting the Ti addition to approximately 1–2 at.% will keep the alloy density nearly constant.
Relative to the unmodified alloy, the Ti-added and aged alloy will exhibit a significant increase in yield strength at approximately 1000°C.
The proposed improvement is expected under sustained high-temperature loading around 1000°C.
The strength improvement may cease if temperature exceeds the precipitate stability range.
Loading conditions that cause precipitate coarsening may eliminate the proposed performance improvement.
